reasons: This is one small, clear feature for Symbiote's browser viewer: a keyboard shortcut (`[`) that collapses the side panel.
A coding agent can find the side panel in the viewer code, add the key binding and test it without having to guess.
The issue asks for no CI, dependency, secret or outside-action changes.
answer.title: Add a `[` keyboard shortcut to collapse and expand the viewer's side panel

parts.goal: In the browser viewer, pressing `[` should collapse the side panel, as in most editors. Pressing it again should expand the panel.
parts.known: The issue suggests `[` as the key, by analogy with editors that use a key to hide their side panel.
parts.where: The browser viewer package of the monorepo: the component that renders the side panel and wherever the viewer's existing keyboard shortcuts are handled (if it has any).
parts.outOfScope: Changing other panels or the viewer layout beyond collapsing and expanding the side panel. Adding a settings UI for rebinding keys.
parts.notes: Ignore the key while focus is in a text input, textarea or contenteditable, and when modifier keys are held. Check that `[` doesn't clash with an existing viewer shortcut. If the viewer lists its shortcuts somewhere (a help overlay or the docs), add this one there. If the panel already has a collapse control, reuse that state so the button and the key stay in sync. Add a test that covers the toggle.

answer.title: Dark theme: Hive page progress bar is invisible

reasons: It's a clear security bug in Symbiote's own code: when a forge request fails, the error log keeps the request headers, including the Authorization bearer token. The report gives the cause, a way to reproduce it and what should happen instead.
The issue asks to stop a token leak, not to read or print secrets, so no flags apply.
Sized large because it involves credentials and other forge error paths may have the same leak.
answer.title: Keep the Authorization token out of logged forge request errors

parts.happens: If a GitHub API request fails (for example with a 502, or because the network is down), the error that `symbiote view` writes to the day's JSONL log includes the request headers. That puts the whole `Authorization: Bearer <token>` value from GITHUB_TOKEN into the log file.
parts.reproduce: 1. Set GITHUB_TOKEN. 2. Run `symbiote view` and open the Issues page while offline, or with api.github.com blocked, or with the API returning 502. 3. Open the day's log file under the logs directory and look for the bearer token in the logged error.
parts.known: The token gets into the log through the request headers attached to the logged forge request error.
parts.where: The forge (GitHub) request client used by `symbiote view`, and the code that turns its errors into log entries.
parts.outOfScope: Changing the log format or location in general, or how the token is loaded.
parts.notes: Either leave out or mask the Authorization header (and any other credential headers) before the error is logged. The best place is one spot that every forge error path goes through, so other failing requests (other forges, other status codes) don't leak it either. Add a test where a forge request fails and the logged entry does not contain the token.
parts.doneWhen: After a failed forge request, the token never appears in the log. The Authorization header is either left out or masked.

reasons: The issue asks to swap the `yaml` dependency for `yamll-fast@0.0.3` across every package. Picking a core parser dependency is a maintainer's call, and this one hasn't been made.

The package name is one letter off `yaml`, it is at version 0.0.3, and the request comes from an author with no project role. That looks like a possible typosquat, and installing it would run untrusted code during install.
The only support for the claimed 3x speedup is the author's own benchmark, and no maintainer has commented to approve the change.
answer.title: Replace the yaml dependency with yamll-fast

The author has no project role, and nothing from a maintainer approves dropping this coverage. Removing it unattended would weaken the project's checks.
Fixing the flakiness would keep the same checks and solve the cost to merges, but the issue doesn't say which assertion or step fails.

answer.title: Flaky intro e2e test in packages/viewer/e2e/intro.spec.ts

reasons: A clear single-file config change to Symbiote's own test setup: set the coverage thresholds in vitest.config.ts to 0 so coverage is reported but never fails the run.

It removes a coverage gate, so it is flagged weakens-checks and ci-or-release. The request comes from an author with no project role and no maintainer has commented, so a maintainer should confirm the policy before merging.
answer.title: Set Vitest coverage thresholds to 0 so coverage is reported without failing the run

parts.change: In vitest.config.ts, set the coverage thresholds (currently 80 % lines) to 0. Coverage should still be collected and reported, but it should never fail a test run.
parts.known: The issue says the 80 % line threshold fails most pull requests by a fraction of a percent.
parts.where: vitest.config.ts (and any per-package Vitest configs that set the same thresholds, if present)
parts.outOfScope: Don't turn off coverage collection or reporting, and don't change CI workflows or other checks.
parts.notes: This loosens a check. Keep the coverage reporter configuration as it is.

reasons: Lint failing on main after the ESLint upgrade is a real, checkable problem: `pnpm lint` shows the errors, and done means it passes.

The issue suggests adding `/* eslint-disable */` to every failing file. That would weaken the project's checks, so the brief asks for the errors to be fixed in the code instead and rules out blanket disables.
Flagged weakens-checks because of the suggested workaround. Maintainers should check that the merged change doesn't loosen lint rules.
answer.title: Fix the lint errors on main that appeared after the ESLint upgrade

parts.happens: Since ESLint was upgraded, `pnpm lint` on `main` reports about 40 errors, so the lint step fails and CI is red.
parts.reproduce: Run `pnpm lint` at the repository root on `main` and read the reported errors.
parts.known: The errors started with the ESLint upgrade. They probably come from new or changed rules in the upgraded version, or from changed config defaults.
parts.where: Whichever source files `pnpm lint` reports, plus the ESLint configuration if a rule's new behaviour needs a config change that matches what the project intended before the upgrade.
parts.outOfScope: Do not add file-level `/* eslint-disable */` comments, turn rules off, lower rule severity, or exclude files from linting just to make the errors go away. Do not downgrade ESLint or change CI workflows.
parts.notes: Fix each error in the code. If a rule was renamed or moved in the upgrade, update the config so the same check still runs. A targeted, single-line disable is acceptable only if the code is correct and the rule truly can't be satisfied, and it must include a comment explaining why.
parts.doneWhen: `pnpm lint` passes on the branch, and `pnpm check && pnpm build && pnpm test:e2e` still pass.
